components.gap: Merin's Lemma 3 (p. 271) is stated for every pair with (E1 perp E2 | +-H)_P. The handbook states and proves it only 'when the likelihoods are positive and finite' (rationality-4-3.tex lines 431-438; annex lines 279-282) and does not treat the other cases that hypothesis admits: (a) with a conjunction of positive probability and a zero or infinite likelihood ratio (a source that excludes or entails H) the product and sum identities hold in extended arithmetic, unproved; (b) with a null source or null conjunction the printed identity fails under the chapter's own L completion (P(H)=1/2, P(E1)=0, P(E2|H)=1/2, P(E2|not-H)=1/4: R_L(E1E2>H)=1 but R_L(E1>H)R_L(E2>H)=2; likewise LL 0 against ln 2), and this is not flagged as a source correction. The standing list (inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02b-p15-024.tex lines 948-950) nevertheless records every theorem and lemma other than Lemma 4 as proved. Owed: the boundary cases of Lemma 3 proved where it holds and the failing cases stated as a correction to the source's unrestricted statement, with the standing entry amended. || The p. 272 paragraph 'Conditional compositionality for conjunction' is not presented or given a standing: Merin's evaluation that Lemma 3 (L and LL) exhibits the gold standard for useful conjunctive compositionality in source position, that the qualitative Theorem 6 presages its usefulness, and his comparative claim that no other familiar measure quite matches this (a claim about D, Q, Z, QL, KO and the other measures, asserted without proof; Theorem thm:p15-w02b-p15-024-ko-transform covers only increasing transforms of L, which is the p. 271 claim). The normative list (inductive-logic-and-confirmation-w02c-p15-027.tex lines 1184-1286, item 6 at 1236-1252) records only that the three homomorphism instances are proved, and the Carnap contrast of the same paragraph. Owed: the claim stated in independent words, classified, and either supported (for instance whether D, Q or Z admit any prior-free composition rule under conditional independence given +-H) or recorded as asserted without proof.

defect_observations: Merin's Theorem 5 is printed as 'If A and B are irrelevant to one another conditionally on B and on not-B, that is, if (A perp C | +-B)'; the handbook reads it as (A perp C | +-B) without recording the slip, although it records the other printed slips (Lemma 3 LL subscript, note 7 logarithm, p. 272 display sign).
The source's KO definition (p. 270) displays the identity (a-b)/(a+b) = (P(EH)-P(E)P(H))/(P(H)P(E not-H)+P(not-H)P(EH)); the handbook gives (a-b)/(a+b) and tanh(R_LL/2) but not the covariance form.

The sufficiency theorem is proved for two simple hypotheses on a finite data space; the source's claim (i)/(ii) citing Savage pp. 128-140 states no such restriction. In the chapter's propositional setting (the data E a proposition) the finite case matches, and the standing list records 'proved in the finite binary case'. Not counted as a gap here.

Checked and confirmed: the handbook's statement that the p. 272 display prints the same stacked comparison sign on both sides is accurate (zoomed page image); the restriction of Theorem 7 to contingent source and target matches the dependency papers' regularity assumption (Crupi, Chater and Tentori 2013 p. 189; Crupi and Tentori 2016 p. 650).
